gollek-ml-recursive-reasoning

The gollek-ml-recursive-reasoning module is Gollek’s package root for GRAM-style recursive reasoning, stochastic latent rollouts, structured reasoning benchmarks, and trainer-facing discrete-token dataset utilities.

Overview

Current scope:

  • recursive-reasoning family metadata
  • rollout/session contracts
  • stochastic latent transition interfaces
  • GRAM-style objective and variational transition primitives
  • reference in-memory rollout/session implementation
  • discrete token projection and rollout evaluation helpers
  • N-Queens and Graph Coloring benchmark adapters
  • benchmark-neutral dataset examples, plans, profiles, splits, epochs, and batches

Installation

<dependency>
    <groupId>tech.kayys.gollek</groupId>
    <artifactId>gollek-ml-recursive-reasoning</artifactId>
    <version>0.1.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
</dependency>

Dataset API

DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanner

Composes profiling, splitting, and epoch construction:

DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanConfig config =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanConfig.stratifiedLengthSorted(
        0.10,
        0.10,
        2026L,
        32,
        64,
        -1
    );

DiscreteTokenDatasetPlan plan =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanner.plan(examples, config);

DiscreteTokenDatasetPlan exposes:

  • profile()
  • split()
  • trainEpoch()
  • validationEpoch()
  • testEpoch()
  • trainPaddingRate()
  • diagnostics()
  • diagnostics(DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanDiagnosticsPolicy)
  • readiness(DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanReadinessGate)
  • fingerprint()
  • verifyFingerprint(DiscreteTokenDatasetFingerprint)
  • verifyFingerprintMetadata(Map<?, ?>)
  • verifyFingerprintMetadataSection(Map<?, ?>)
  • verifyFingerprintMetadataSection(Map<?, ?>, String)
  • report()
  • report(DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanReadinessGate)

DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanConfig selects:

  • DiscreteTokenDatasetSplitMode
  • DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainEpochMode
  • split seed
  • training/evaluation batch sizes
  • input/target pad tokens
  • train dropLast policy

DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanDiagnostics exposes:

  • isReadyForTraining()
  • status()
  • hasWarnings()
  • warnings()
  • knownSolutionCoverageRate()
  • trainPaddingRate()
  • trainPaddingTokenCount()
  • droppedTrainingExamples()
  • taskSplits()
  • toMetadata()

DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanDiagnosticsPolicy controls optional warnings:

  • defaults() keeps the standard pre-training checks
  • lenient() suppresses optional warnings while preserving hard blockers
  • withHighPaddingRateThreshold(...) tunes padding sensitivity for CI or production trainers
  • withEvaluationSplitWarnings(...), withKnownSolutionWarnings(...), withPerTaskSplitWarnings(...), and withPaddingWarning(...) toggle common warning groups
  • fromMetadata(...) and toMetadata() round-trip persisted trainer or CI warning policies

DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanReadinessGate converts diagnostics into run control:

  • training() accepts trainable plans while preserving warning metadata
  • strict() rejects trainable plans that still have warnings
  • lenient() evaluates with lenient diagnostics first
  • evaluate(...), requireReady(...), and plan.readiness(...) produce a DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanReadinessReport
  • fromMetadata(...) and toMetadata() round-trip the selected diagnostics policy and warning-failure mode

DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanReadinessReport exposes accepted(), gateStatus(), rejectionReasons(), requireAccepted(), and toMetadata().

DiscreteTokenDatasetFingerprint provides stable SHA-256 provenance:

  • fromExamples(...) hashes ordered token examples and metadata
  • fromPlan(...) and plan.fingerprint() hash config, splits, examples, and materialized epoch layout
  • fromMetadata(...), fromMetadataSection(...), shortValue(), shortValue(length), and toMetadata() support compact reports and checkpoint metadata

DiscreteTokenDatasetFingerprintMatch verifies checkpoint/resume provenance:

  • verify(expected, actual), verify(expected, plan), and verify(expected, report) compare stored and current fingerprints
  • plan.verifyFingerprint(expected) and report.verifyFingerprint(expected) provide convenient resume guards
  • verifyMetadata(...), plan.verifyFingerprintMetadata(...), and report.verifyFingerprintMetadata(...) accept stored checkpoint metadata
  • verifyMetadataSection(...), plan.verifyFingerprintMetadataSection(...), and report.verifyFingerprintMetadataSection(...) extract nested fingerprint metadata from full report/checkpoint payloads
  • matches(), status(), mismatchReasons(), summary(), requireMatch(), and toMetadata() support fail-fast resume checks and CI payloads

DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanReport is the combined preflight bundle:

  • from(plan), from(plan, gate), plan.report(), and plan.report(gate) assemble fingerprint plus readiness metadata
  • diagnostics(), accepted(), gateStatus(), warnings(), and requireAccepted() provide one-call trainer checks
  • summary() and toMetadata() are designed for logs, CI payloads, and checkpoint provenance

DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointManifest is the trainer checkpoint wrapper:

  • builder(report) creates a manifest with experiment, run, model family, seed, checkpoint step, creator, timestamp, and custom attributes
  • fingerprint(), datasetAccepted(), datasetGateStatus(), verifyPlan(...), verifyReport(...), and requireDatasetAccepted() support resume checks around the stored dataset plan
  • toMetadata() emits top-level checkpoint fields plus a top-level fingerprint section and nested datasetPlanReport

DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointManifestSnapshot is the read-side checkpoint view:

  • fromMetadata(...) and fromManifest(...) rehydrate persisted manifest metadata without rebuilding the original plan report
  • isCurrentSchema(), requireCurrentSchema(), datasetPlanReportFingerprint(), verifyPlan(...), verifyReport(...), and requireDatasetAccepted() support fail-fast resume guards
  • resumeReport(plan) and resumeReport(report) combine schema, readiness, and fingerprint checks into one checkpoint-resume report
  • overloads of resumeReport(...) accept a DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeExpectation for stricter experiment identity checks
  • toMetadata() round-trips the manifest payload and checks that top-level fingerprint/readiness fields still match the nested datasetPlanReport

DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeExpectation is the optional identity guard for resume paths:

  • none(), builder(), exactFromManifest(...), and exactFromSnapshot(...) create expectations for experiment name, run id, model family, seed, exact checkpoint step, or minimum checkpoint step
  • active(), accepts(snapshot), rejectionReasons(snapshot), and toMetadata() make expectation failures explainable in trainer reports

DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumePolicy is the trainer-facing resume gate:

  • training(), strict(), and lenient() select the current plan readiness gate used during resume
  • withCurrentPlanGate(...) and withExpectation(...) customize the policy
  • fromMetadata(...) and toMetadata() round-trip persisted resume policy settings, including the current readiness gate and expectation
  • evaluate(...) and requireReady(...) accept checkpoint metadata, a manifest, or a snapshot plus the freshly materialized plan, then return a DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeReport

DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeReport is the one-call resume preflight:

  • fromMetadata(...) and fromSnapshot(...) compare a persisted checkpoint manifest with a freshly materialized plan or plan report
  • schemaAccepted(), datasetAccepted(), fingerprintMatched(), ready(), status(), rejectionReasons(), summary(), and requireReady() make checkpoint resume failures reportable and fail-fast
  • gateSummary(), gates(), gatesById(), gate(...), gateAccepted(...), requireGateAccepted(...), requireAllGatesAccepted(), blockedGates(), and warningGates() expose stable aggregate and per-guard decisions for automation and extension preflights
  • actionPlan(), readinessBadge(), nextActions(), primaryAction(), requiredActions(), warningActions(), actionCodes(), requiredActionCodes(), warningActionCodes(), and requireNoRequiredActions() provide direct access to the resume action handoff without traversing gateSummary()
  • currentPlanChecked(), currentPlanAccepted(), and currentPlanGateStatus() report whether the current plan/report still passes
  • explanation() derives stable finding codes, categories, details, and next steps. DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeExplanation.fromMetadata(...) and requireMetadataMatch(...) rehydrate and validate that explanation payload for CI, dashboards, and extension consumers.
  • DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeCompatibilityMode supports STRICT, COMPATIBLE, and explicit FORCE resume decisions. Force decisions can return ready while still carrying compatibility warnings.
  • policyTracked() and policyMetadata() show whether a reusable resume policy produced the report and expose that serialized policy for audit logs
  • toMetadata() exports the resume decision, fingerprint match payload, and checkpoint snapshot, plus per-gate decisions, the current plan report, and policy snapshot when available, for CI and trainer reports

DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeGate is the stable per-guard decision used inside resume reports and snapshots:

  • Gate ids cover checkpoint manifest schema, checkpoint dataset readiness, dataset fingerprint, resume expectation, and current dataset plan readiness
  • accepted(), blocked(), warning(), attentionRequired(), actionRequired(), status(), severity(), actionCode(), actionHint(), requireAccepted(), details(), and toMetadata() let CI and extensions enforce one guard without parsing human-readable summaries

DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeGateSummary is the compact aggregate used for dashboards and CI logs:

  • status(), allAccepted(), attentionRequired(), actionRequired(), highestSeverity(), gateCount(), acceptedCount(), blockedCount(), warningCount(), blockedGateIds(), warningGateIds(), gatesByStatus(), gatesBySeverity(), gatesByCategory(), gateIdsByStatus(), gateIdsBySeverity(), gateIdsByCategory(), gateCountByStatus(), gateCountBySeverity(), gateCountByCategory(), gateCategorySummaries(), gateCategorySummaryByCategory(), gateCategorySummary(...), requireGateCategorySummary(...), categoryIds(), acceptedCategories(), blockedCategories(), warningCategories(), acceptedCategorySummaries(), blockedCategorySummaries(), warningCategorySummaries(), primaryBlockedCategorySummary(), primaryWarningCategorySummary(), primaryBlockedCategory(), primaryWarningCategory(), primaryBlockedGate(), primaryWarningGate(), primaryGate(), primaryGateId(), primaryGateCategory(), primaryGateStatus(), primaryGateSeverity(), primaryActionCode(), primaryActionHint(), primaryAction(), nextActions(), requiredActions(), warningActions(), actionCodes(), requiredActionCodes(), warningActionCodes(), actionPlan(), readinessBadge(), requireAllAccepted(), and toMetadata() summarize the full gate list without losing the primary blocker, warning identity, category rollups, category status lists, or grouped machine-readable gate indexes and automation-safe next action

DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeActionPlan is the one-object handoff for resume automation and UI integrations:

  • status(), ready(), readyWithoutWarnings(), attentionRequired(), actionRequired(), actionCount(), requiredActionCount(), warningActionCount(), primaryActionCode(), primaryActionHint(), primaryGateId(), primaryCategory(), actionCodes(), requiredActionCodes(), warningActionCodes(), actions(), requiredActions(), warningActions(), primaryAction(), summary(), requireNoRequiredActions(), fromMetadata(...), and toMetadata() expose a compact action plan without requiring each consumer to combine summary fields by hand

DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeAction is the ordered action item derived from the resume gate summary:

  • rank(), code(), hint(), gateId(), category(), status(), severity(), primary(), attentionRequired(), actionRequired(), blocked(), warning(), gateSummary(), fromMetadata(...), and toMetadata() let CI, dashboards, and operator tools render a prioritized resume repair/review plan without re-sorting gates
  • nextActions() returns blocked actions first, warning actions second, and a single continue action only when the checkpoint is already ready

DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeReadinessBadge is the render-friendly headline status for CLI, CI, and dashboards:

  • status(), label(), tone(), severity(), iconKey(), attentionRequired(), actionRequired(), primaryMessage(), actionCode(), actionHint(), primaryGateId(), primaryGateCategory(), primaryGateStatus(), primaryGateSeverity(), ready(), blocked(), warning(), fromMetadata(...), and toMetadata() condense the full gate summary into one stable UI payload. actionCode() is stable for automation, while actionHint() is display text for operators.

DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeGateCategorySummary is the compact per-category rollup used by the aggregate summary:

  • category(), status(), severity(), allAccepted(), gateCount(), attentionRequired(), actionRequired(), acceptedCount(), blockedCount(), warningCount(), gateIds(), blockedGateIds(), warningGateIds(), primaryGate(), primaryBlockedGate(), primaryWarningGate(), primaryActionCode(), primaryActionHint(), summary(), fromMetadata(...), requireMetadataMatch(...), and toMetadata() let dashboards render and validate one stable row per resume guard category

DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeReportSnapshot is the read-side resume audit view:

  • fromReport(...) and fromMetadata(...) rehydrate persisted resume-report JSON without needing the current dataset plan
  • requireReady(), summary(), gateSummary(), actionPlan(), readinessBadge(), gates(), gateAccepted(...), requireGateAccepted(...), requireAllGatesAccepted(), requireNoRequiredActions(), toMetadata(), policyMetadata(), and currentPlanReportMetadata() support CI gates, dashboards, and extension tooling that inspect completed checkpoint preflights
  • persisted gateSummary, top-level actionPlan, and top-level readinessBadge metadata are validated against the detailed gates when present, including grouped gate indexes when present, while older sidecars without gate fields synthesize the current gate list from the legacy resume booleans and fingerprint payload

DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointSnapshot is the checkpoint-directory audit view:

  • read(checkpointDir) loads the manifest sidecar plus the optional resume report sidecar in one call
  • manifestReady(), resumeReportPresent(), resumeReady(), ready(), and status() distinguish manifest-only, ready, and blocked checkpoint states
  • requireReady(), requireResumeReport(), requireResumeReady(), trainingReportMetadata(), and toMetadata() give dashboards and extensions a compact checkpoint audit payload

DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointInventory scans checkpoint roots:

  • scan(rootDir) reads the root checkpoint, if present, plus immediate child checkpoint directories that contain the dataset manifest sidecar
  • checkpointCount(), readyCount(), blockedCount(), manifestOnlyCount(), resumeReportCount(), and failureCount() summarize checkpoint health for dashboards and CI
  • latestCheckpoint(), latestReadyCheckpoint(), requireLatestReadyCheckpoint(), requireNoFailures(), summary(), and toMetadata() expose an inventory payload while preserving corrupt sidecars as read failures instead of aborting the whole scan
  • selectCheckpoint(policy) and requireCheckpoint(policy) delegate restore choice to a reusable checkpoint selection policy
  • selectRestorePlan(policy) and requireRestorePlan(policy) return the same choice as a typed restore-plan handoff for trainer resume code
  • DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointLineageGraph.fromInventory(...) resolves root-to-leaf checkpoint ancestry and reports duplicate run ids, missing-parent references, ambiguous parent links, parent identity mismatches, and lineage cycles
  • healthy(), healthMetadata(), healthSnapshot(), issueTypes(), issueDetails(), and requireHealthy() provide a compact CI/dashboard health gate over the graph with stable issue codes, severity, blocking status, affected checkpoint paths, issue-specific reasons, remediation actions, issueDetailCount, blockingIssueCount, plus top-level kind and schemaVersion fields for the stable health payload contract
  • DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointLineageHealthSnapshot.fromMetadata(...) rehydrates that payload for extensions, CI jobs, and dashboards that should not parse raw maps by hand; it also round-trips with toMetadata(), exposes primary issue/failing-check convenience accessors, and validates the current gollek.checkpoint-lineage-health.v1 contract
  • DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointLineageHealthValidationReport.fromMetadata(...), fromJson(...), and fromPath(...) return a dependency-free checkpoint-lineage-health-validation payload with stable valid/invalid status, error codes, and compact health summaries for CI or extension handoffs; fromValidationMetadata(...), fromValidationJson(...), and fromValidationPath(...) rehydrate a persisted validation report, and jsonSchemaMetadata() exposes its bundled schema contract
  • DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointLineageHealthSchemaCatalog.catalogMetadata(...) publishes the lineage-health schema catalog, including the health payload contract, validation-report contract, schema ids, resources, and inspector section names, plus schemaSetSha256, per-schema SHA-256 digests, and byte counts for drift checks; jsonSchemaMetadata() exposes the schema-catalog contract itself, while lockMetadata() and lockJsonSchemaMetadata() expose a compact lock payload and its schema, lockSnapshot() exposes the same payload through typed lock accessors, and validateLockMetadata(...) returns a stable valid/invalid report for saved lock drift checks; validateLockJson(...) and validateLockPath(...) cover persisted lock text/files, validateLockSnapshot(...) covers rehydrated lock snapshots, requireValidLockMetadata(...), requireValidLockJson(...), and requireValidLockPath(...) fail fast on drift, while lockValidationJsonSchemaMetadata() exposes that validation report schema. The report carries its validation schema id/resource and expected/actual lock-schema ids for self-describing CI artifacts
  • DiscreteTokenDatasetSchemaCatalogSnapshot wraps schema-catalog metadata with typed accessors such as schemaSetSha256(), schemaSetIdentity(), matchesSchemaSet(...), requireSchemaSet(...), contractNames(), contract(...), contractDetails(), contractsByName(), contractDetail(...), requireContract(...), requireContractDetail(...), contractsByJsonSchemaId(), contractForJsonSchemaId(...), requireContractForJsonSchemaId(...), contractsByPayloadKind(), contractsForPayloadKind(...), contractForPayloadSchema(...), requireContractForPayloadSchema(...), hasEmbeddedSchemas(), and requireCurrentSchema(...), while preserving compact or embedded-schema catalog metadata through toMetadata()
  • DiscreteTokenDatasetSchemaLockSnapshot wraps schema-lock metadata with typed accessors such as schemaSetSha256(), schemaCount(), schemaSetIdentity(), matchesSchemaSet(...), requireSchemaSet(...), contractNames(), contract(...), contractDetails(), contractsByName(), contractDetail(...), requireContract(...), requireContractDetail(...), contractsByJsonSchemaId(), contractForJsonSchemaId(...), requireContractForJsonSchemaId(...), contractsByPayloadKind(), contractsForPayloadKind(...), contractForPayloadSchema(...), requireContractForPayloadSchema(...), and requireCurrentSchema(...), while preserving the original lock metadata through toMetadata()
  • DiscreteTokenDatasetSchemaContractSnapshot wraps one schema catalog or lock contract entry with accessors for payload schema identity, JSON schema id, SHA-256 digest, byte count, optional catalog metadata, embedded schema metadata, and raw toMetadata() access
  • DiscreteTokenDatasetSchemaSetIdentity wraps the shared schema-set SHA-256 digest and schema count so catalogs, locks, and validation reports can compare schema identity through matches(...), requireMatches(...), and toMetadata()
  • DiscreteTokenDatasetSchemaLockValidationReport wraps schema-lock validation metadata with typed accessors such as valid(), mismatchCount(), expectedSchemaSetIdentity(), actualSchemaSetIdentity(), schemaSetIdentityMatch(), requireSchemaSetIdentityMatch(), mismatchPaths(), mismatchDetails(), firstMismatch(), and hasMismatchAtPath(...), plus mismatchesForPath(...), mismatchesForType(...), mismatchesByPath(), mismatchesByType(), and requireValid() while preserving the original validation metadata through toMetadata()
  • DiscreteTokenDatasetSchemaLockMismatch wraps one schema-lock validation mismatch with type(), path(), expected(), actual(), summary(), and raw toMetadata() access for CI logs and extension diagnostics
  • DiscreteTokenDatasetSchemaContract is the reusable schema descriptor used to load bundled JSON Schema resources, compute SHA-256 digests and byte counts, and render standard contract metadata with optional embedded schemas
  • DiscreteTokenDatasetSchemaBundle composes reusable schema contracts into the common catalog, compact lock, and lock-validation report surface used by lineage-health schema drift checks, giving future trainer artifacts the same CI-friendly schema-lock mechanics without duplicating catalog comparison code; use builder(...) for new bundles so catalog/lock/validator fields stay explicit and duplicate contract names fail during bundle construction
  • DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointLineageHealthSnapshot.jsonSchemaMetadata() exposes the bundled JSON Schema contract (checkpoint-lineage-health.v1.schema.json) for schema-aware extension registries, CI validators, and dashboard parsers
  • status(), primaryIssue(), primaryIssueCode(), primaryIssueType(), and primaryIssueAction() expose a deterministic headline issue for CI summaries when the graph is unhealthy
  • healthScore(), alertLevel(), recommendedAction(), and healthBadge() expose a UI-ready status projection for dashboards and trainer reports
  • checks(), failingChecks(), passingCheckCount(), failingCheckCount(), primaryFailingCheck(), primaryFailingCheckCode(), primaryFailingCheckType(), primaryFailingCheckAction(), primaryFailingCheckSeverity(), primaryFailingCheckMessage(), and checkSummary() expose category-level invariant rows for duplicate run ids, parent resolution, parent identity, and cycles, including primary failing-check identity, type, action, full check payload, and severity rollups; healthMetadata() mirrors the priority-aware primary failing-check fields at the top level when a check fails

DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointSelectionPolicy chooses checkpoints from an inventory:

  • latestReady() selects the latest ready checkpoint and accepts manifest-only directories
  • latestResumeReady() selects the latest ready checkpoint that also has a persisted ready resume report
  • strictLatestReady() and strictLatestResumeReady() reject inventories with corrupt sidecar reads before selecting a checkpoint
  • withFailOnLineageIssues(true) rejects unhealthy lineage graphs before selecting a checkpoint; this covers duplicate run ids, missing parents, ambiguous parents, parent identity mismatches, and cycles
  • withExpectation(...), candidates(...), rejectionReasons(...), toMetadata(), and fromMetadata(...) support trainer config, dashboards, and CI restore gates

DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointInspectionReport explains a selection decision:

  • inspect(rootDir, policy) and inspect(inventory, policy) scan or reuse an inventory and apply the selection policy
  • selectedCheckpoint(), selectionFailure(), selectionSatisfied(), acceptedCount(), rejectedCount(), and checkpointDecisions() expose the restore result and all candidate decisions
  • strict policies keep candidate decisions visible while recording inventory read failures as selection blockers
  • toMetadata() exports a JSON-friendly payload for JBang inspectors, dashboards, and CI restore gates
  • selectedRestorePlan() and requireRestorePlan() expose the selected checkpoint as a typed restore-plan handoff
  • lineageGraph(), selectedLineageChain(), and requireSelectedLineageChain() expose resolved checkpoint ancestry without forcing tools to parse every manifest sidecar

DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointRestorePlan packages a selected checkpoint for resume handoff:

  • fromInspectionReport(report) and fromCheckpoint(root, checkpoint, policy) create restore plans from existing selection surfaces
  • checkpointDir(), manifestPath(), resumeReportPath(), manifest(), and resumeReport() give resume code direct typed access to the selected sidecars
  • requireReady(), requireResumeReport(), and requireResumeReady() keep fail-fast restore guards near the selected checkpoint
  • pathsMetadata(), identityMetadata(), summary(), and toMetadata() emit compact CLI, dashboard, and extension handoff payloads

DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointRestorePreflight validates a selected restore plan against the current trainer dataset plan:

  • evaluate(restorePlan, currentPlan, resumePolicy) creates the current-plan preflight report for an already selected checkpoint
  • ready(), status(), rejectionReasons(), and requireReady() expose the final resume decision before model or optimizer state is opened
  • gates(), gateSummary(), nextActions(), primaryAction(), requiredActions(), warningActions(), actionCodes(), requiredActionCodes(), warningActionCodes(), actionPlan(), readinessBadge(), requireAllGatesAccepted(), requireNoRequiredActions(), and requireMetadataMatch(...) mirror the resume-report action handoff and validate live restore metadata
  • toMetadata() keeps the selected restore plan, resume policy, and current resume report together for dashboards and CI gates, including top-level actionPlan and readinessBadge aliases

DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointMetadataJson persists checkpoint/resume metadata without adding a JSON dependency:

  • toJson(...) and toPrettyJson(...) emit deterministic JSON with sorted object keys for stable diffs and golden fixtures
  • fromJson(...) reads metadata maps back into immutable Java maps/lists
  • write(path, manifest), write(path, metadata), read(path), and readSnapshot(path) cover trainer checkpoint manifest files
  • readPlanReport(path) rehydrates a persisted dataset plan report from JSON
  • readResumeReportSnapshot(path) rehydrates persisted resume-report JSON

DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerProvenanceSpec is the one-object trainer setup:

  • builder(checkpointDir, plan) materializes the plan report, checkpoint manifest, resume policy, sidecar paths, bridge helpers, and listener wiring
  • strict(), lenient(), gate(...), resumeGate(...), and exactResumeExpectation() configure the write-side and resume-side checks
  • writeManifest(), requireResumeReadyAndWriteReport(), listener(), and attachToTrainingSummary(...) expose the normal checkpoint lifecycle without rebuilding the manifest/policy/listener by hand
  • checkpointRootDir(), restoreSelectionPolicy(), inspectRestoreCandidates(), selectRestorePlan(), requireRestorePlan(), evaluateRestorePreflight(), and requireRestorePreflightReady() expose the read-side restore target and final current-plan preflight using the same resume expectation carried by the spec
  • toMetadata() exports the complete provenance setup for trainer config, CI, and dashboards

DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointBridge is the trainer integration helper:

  • manifestPath(checkpointDir) and resumeReportPath(checkpointDir) define stable sidecar names inside a trainer checkpoint directory
  • writeManifest(...), readManifestMetadata(...), and readSnapshot(...) persist and reload dataset provenance beside model/optimizer checkpoints
  • readResumeReportMetadata(...) and readResumeReportSnapshot(...) reload the resume audit sidecar after a preflight has run
  • readCheckpointSnapshot(...) loads the full checkpoint-directory sidecar state, including manifest-only directories
  • scanCheckpointInventory(...) scans a checkpoint root and returns ready, blocked, manifest-only, and failed sidecar reads in one inventory object
  • selectCheckpoint(...) and requireCheckpoint(...) scan a checkpoint root and apply a reusable checkpoint selection policy
  • inspectCheckpoints(...) scans a checkpoint root and returns a full checkpoint inspection report with selected checkpoint, candidate decisions, and inventory read failures
  • selectRestorePlan(...) and requireRestorePlan(...) scan a checkpoint root and return the selected checkpoint as a typed resume handoff
  • evaluateRestorePreflight(...) and requireRestorePreflightReady(...) validate a selected restore target against the current dataset plan before state is loaded
  • evaluateResume(...), requireResumeReady(...), and requireResumeReadyAndWriteReport(...) run the resume policy from persisted metadata and optionally write an audit JSON report
  • attachToTrainingMetadata(...) and attachToTrainingSummary(...) add a recursiveReasoningDataset section to trainer-facing metadata/summary maps

DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerProvenanceListener wires that bridge into trainer lifecycle callbacks:

  • create(...) writes the dataset manifest when training starts
  • withResumePreflight(...) and builder(...) preflight an existing sidecar before overwriting it, failing fast on fingerprint/policy rejection by default
  • lastResumeReport(), lastEnrichedSummary(), and trainingReportMetadata() expose the resume audit and summary metadata after callbacks run

DiscreteTokenDatasetTaskSplitDiagnostics provides per-task train, validation, and test counts plus split rates for mixed benchmark datasets.

DiscreteTokenDatasetExample

Canonical single example for structured reasoning trainers.

Constructor fields:

new DiscreteTokenDatasetExample(
    String taskId,
    int exampleIndex,
    int[] inputTokens,
    int[] targetTokens,
    int knownSolutionCount,
    Map<String, Object> metadata
)

Validation:

  • taskId must not be blank
  • exampleIndex >= 0
  • input and target tokens must be non-empty
  • knownSolutionCount must be -1 or >= 1
  • token arrays are defensively copied

DiscreteTokenDatasetProfiler

Builds compact dataset diagnostics:

DiscreteTokenDatasetProfile profile =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetProfiler.profile(examples);

Main profile fields:

  • exampleCount()
  • taskExampleCounts()
  • inputLengths()
  • targetLengths()
  • observedTokenCount()
  • distinctTokenCount()
  • minToken()
  • maxToken()
  • knownSolutionCoverageRate()

DiscreteTokenDatasetSplitter

Deterministic train/validation/test splits:

DiscreteTokenDatasetSplit split =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetSplitter.shuffledByFractions(
        examples,
        0.10,
        0.10,
        2026L
    );

Available split policies:

Method Policy
sequentialByCounts exact validation/test counts, source order
shuffledByCounts exact validation/test counts, seeded shuffle
sequentialByFractions floor-fraction validation/test sizes, source order
shuffledByFractions floor-fraction validation/test sizes, seeded shuffle
stratifiedSequentialByFractions floor fractions inside each taskId, source order
stratifiedShuffledByFractions floor fractions inside each taskId, seeded shuffle

DiscreteTokenDatasetSplit exposes:

  • trainExamples()
  • validationExamples()
  • testExamples()
  • profile()
  • trainProfile()
  • validationProfile()
  • testProfile()
  • trainEpoch(...)
  • validationEpoch(...)
  • testEpoch(...)

DiscreteTokenDatasetEpochBatcher

Materializes mini-batches:

DiscreteTokenDatasetEpoch epoch =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetEpochBatcher.lengthSorted(
        split.trainExamples(),
        32,
        -1,
        false
    );

Available epoch policies:

Method Policy
sequential source order mini-batches
shuffled seeded shuffled mini-batches
lengthSorted combined input/target length sorting to reduce padding

DiscreteTokenDatasetEpoch exposes:

  • batches()

  • emittedExampleCount()
  • droppedExampleCount()
  • observedTokenCount()
  • paddedTokenCapacity()
  • paddingTokenCount()
  • paddingRate()

DiscreteTokenDatasetBatcher

Pads examples into one batch:

DiscreteTokenDatasetBatch batch =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetBatcher.batch(examples, -1, -1);

DiscreteTokenDatasetBatch exposes:

  • taskIds()

  • targetMask()

Structured Benchmark APIs

N-Queens:

  • NQueensProblem
  • NQueensSolution
  • NQueensDatasetGenerator
  • NQueensTokenCodec
  • NQueensTokenProjector
  • NQueensRolloutEvaluator

Graph Coloring:

  • GraphColoringProblem
  • GraphColoringSolution
  • GraphColoringDatasetGenerator
  • GraphColoringTokenCodec
  • GraphColoringTokenProjector
  • GraphColoringRolloutEvaluator

Both benchmark families can emit DiscreteTokenDatasetExample through their dataset-example adapters.

Example

List<DiscreteTokenDatasetExample> examples = List.of(
    graphColoringExample.toTokenExample(),
    nQueensExample.toTokenExample()
);

DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanConfig config =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanConfig.stratifiedLengthSorted(
        0.10,
        0.10,
        2026L,
        32,
        64,
        -1
    );

DiscreteTokenDatasetPlan plan =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanner.plan(examples, config);

DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanDiagnostics diagnostics = plan.diagnostics();
DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanDiagnostics ciDiagnostics = plan.diagnostics(
    DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanDiagnosticsPolicy.defaults()
        .withHighPaddingRateThreshold(0.25)
);
DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanReadinessReport readiness = plan.readiness(
    DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanReadinessGate.strict()
);
DiscreteTokenDatasetFingerprint fingerprint = plan.fingerprint();
Map<String, Object> checkpointFingerprintMetadata = fingerprint.toMetadata();
DiscreteTokenDatasetFingerprint expectedFingerprint =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetFingerprint.fromMetadata(checkpointFingerprintMetadata);
DiscreteTokenDatasetFingerprintMatch resumeMatch =
    plan.verifyFingerprint(expectedFingerprint);
DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanReport report = plan.report(
    DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanReadinessGate.strict()
);
Map<String, Object> metadata = report.toMetadata();
report.verifyFingerprintMetadataSection(metadata).requireMatch();
Path checkpointDir = Path.of("checkpoints/run-001");
DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerProvenanceSpec provenance =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerProvenanceSpec.builder(checkpointDir, plan)
        .strict()
        .experimentName("gram-structured-reasoning")
        .runId("run-001")
        .seed(2026L)
        .checkpointStep(12L)
        .exactResumeExpectation()
        .build();
DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointManifest manifest = provenance.manifest();
Map<String, Object> checkpointMetadata = manifest.toMetadata();
provenance.writeManifest();
Map<String, Object> loadedCheckpointMetadata = provenance.readManifestMetadata();
DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointManifestSnapshot snapshot =
    provenance.readSnapshot();
snapshot.requireCurrentSchema();
snapshot.verifyPlan(plan).requireMatch();
snapshot.requireDatasetAccepted();
DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeReport resumeReport =
    snapshot.resumeReport(plan);
resumeReport.requireReady();
DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeExpectation expectedCheckpoint =
    provenance.resumeExpectation();
snapshot.resumeReport(plan, expectedCheckpoint).requireReady();
DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanReport currentStrictReport =
    plan.report(DiscreteTokenDatasetPlanReadinessGate.strict());
snapshot.resumeReport(currentStrictReport, expectedCheckpoint).requireReady();
DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumePolicy resumePolicy =
    provenance.resumePolicy();
DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeReport policyReport =
    provenance.requireResumeReadyAndWriteReport();
DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumeReportSnapshot persistedResumeAudit =
    provenance.readResumeReportSnapshot();
persistedResumeAudit.requireReady();
DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointSnapshot checkpointAudit =
    provenance.readCheckpointSnapshot();
checkpointAudit.requireReady();
DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointInventory checkpointInventory =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointInventory.scan(checkpointDir.getParent());
DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointSnapshot latestReadyCheckpoint =
    checkpointInventory.requireLatestReadyCheckpoint();
DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointSelectionPolicy checkpointSelection =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointSelectionPolicy.latestResumeReady()
        .withExpectation(provenance.resumeExpectation());
DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointSnapshot latestResumeReadyCheckpoint =
    checkpointSelection.require(checkpointInventory);
DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointSnapshot bridgeSelectedCheckpoint =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointBridge.requireCheckpoint(
        checkpointDir.getParent(),
        checkpointSelection);
DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointRestorePlan restorePlan =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointBridge.requireRestorePlan(
        checkpointDir.getParent(),
        checkpointSelection);
DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointRestorePreflight restorePreflight =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointBridge.requireRestorePreflightReady(
        restorePlan,
        plan,
        provenance.resumePolicy());
DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointRestorePlan provenanceRestorePlan =
    provenance.requireRestorePlan();
DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerCheckpointRestorePreflight provenanceRestorePreflight =
    provenance.requireRestorePreflightReady();
Map<String, Object> resumeAuditMetadata = policyReport.toMetadata();
Map<String, Object> trainerMetadata =
    provenance.attachToTrainingMetadata(Map.of("runId", "run-001"), policyReport);
DiscreteTokenDatasetTrainerProvenanceListener provenanceListener =
    provenance.listener();
// Pass provenanceListener to a canonical trainer via .listener(provenanceListener).
TrainingSummary enrichedSummary =
    provenanceListener.lastEnrichedSummary().orElse(null);
Map<String, Object> resumePolicyMetadata = resumePolicy.toMetadata();
DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumePolicy reloadedResumePolicy =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointResumePolicy.fromMetadata(resumePolicyMetadata);
reloadedResumePolicy.requireReady(loadedCheckpointMetadata, plan);
String resumeAuditJson =
    DiscreteTokenDatasetCheckpointMetadataJson.toPrettyJson(resumeAuditMetadata);
List<DiscreteTokenDatasetTaskSplitDiagnostics> taskSplits =
    diagnostics.taskSplits();
DiscreteTokenDatasetBatch firstBatch = plan.trainEpoch().batches().get(0);
